summary: The comment opposes limiting or sunsetting E-Rate, citing potential increased costs for schools and libraries in maintaining broadband infrastructure. The text discusses concerns about the impact of mobile phones on health, particularly brain cancer risk, and suggests limiting or sunsetting E-Rate programs could lead to increased costs for schools and libraries. The text discusses the effects of electromagnetic radiation on cell proliferation and other cellular processes. It mentions the use of a mast cell line, RBL 2H3, to investigate the effects of exposure to electromagnetic radiation at a frequency used by mobile phone communication on a range of cellular processes. The study demonstrates that exposure to 835 MHz microwaves elicits alterations in cell proliferation, F-actin distribution, cell morphology, and secretion in RBL-2H3 cells. The text also The FCC comment opposes sunset clauses for E-Rate programs, arguing against their statutory authority.
filer_raw: Kevin Mottus | Outreach Director, CA Brain Tumor Assn
